It occurred to me that there might be an opportunity to support voat and needier people too – because it's not a zero-sum game. Picture this:

  1. Users buy VoatGoats (or fractions thereof EDIT: alternative name: Goat Certificates), which could be similar to reddit gold, except:

That money is used to micro-invest, to extend microcredits to people who are trying to better their business, especially in developing countries (if nothing else, then for the practical reason that a small loan will go a lot further there). Maybe some will better their business by buying actual goats.

  3. Depending on the success of those microcredits, some of, all of, or even all of the money plus a modest interest will return to voat, where it then pays for servers and keeping the lights on.

Wouldn't this freemium approach basically mean, the more you pay, the more votes you get? More money, more influence? You know, like in American politics? I'm not trying to put you down, and I appreciate that you appreciated my idea, but I think this could be a problem.

Short version: I concede the point after thinking through some of the details, but will leave it up for the fostering of good discussion.

Long version: You are correct about my idea - it sets up a system where money can buy influence. The only difference is that I am advocating two forms of currency that can 'purchase' influence. You can buy more votes with money, or by contributing meaningfully to discussions. In this case being corrupt and 'buying' influence still leads to a greater good of funding the site.

My idea would have had merit if any single human could only upvoat or downvoat any given post once. That would put the two currencies on a level playing field, with a slight advantage to the earned quota since paying for the quota increases it only for the day. If you wanted to keep your paid advantage, you have to keep paying and paying and paying. Whereas the work put in to be a better Voater and contribute permantly increases your quota.

While not necessarily ideal, this system I think would be a fair compromise that has the potential to keep itself in check and realistically fund the site.

However, the flaw in my proposal that I missed, which is an offshoot of your comment is: that a single human can have multiple accounts and thusly upvoat or downvoat a single post multiple times. What's to stop someone from upvoating all of their own comments on all of their accounts with each of their multiple accounts? Suddenly that single human has enough influence and can 'in theory' single handedly bring garbage content to the front page by buying influence or cheating the system.

So in the end, you're right. but i appreciate the challenge and thanks for making me think this through at a deeper level.
